key_insight: Training a Mamba-based language model with targeted data augmentation and an experience-replay memory lets the model generate property-optimized small molecules far more sample-efficiently than standard approaches.
problem_solved: Designing molecules with desired properties typically requires large datasets and many expensive evaluations or simulations; this work reduces the data and compute needed to discover high-quality candidate molecules.
method: Train a Mamba-based generative language model tailored to molecular SMILES/representations.
Apply targeted data augmentation to expand effective training signals without new experiments.
Use experience-replay (memory manipulation) to retain and re-use promising samples during optimization, boosting sample efficiency for property-guided generation.
impact: Enables faster, lower-cost molecular design workflows by reducing the number of evaluations and training data required—accelerating iteration in drug discovery and materials design for ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Mamba LM → data augmentation → experience replay memory → property scorer → generated molecules

paper_title: Sample-efficient generative molecular design using memory manipulation
paper_authors: Jeff Guo, Junwu Chen, Anthony GX-Chen, Philippe Schwaller
